findings.whatIsWrong: The claimed post-migration taxonomy, 688-row classification manifest, 50 semantic pool indexes, and AI content guide are absent from the checked-out branch. The latest reachable commit is the prior audit commit a0525079, not a Gemini migration commit.
findings.whyItMatters: There is no canonical classification layer to validate or consume. The 688-question taxonomy is not implemented, and the future-AI contract claimed by Gemini cannot be audited or used.
findings.recommendedCorrection: Do not freeze or extend the taxonomy. Supply or implement the claimed artifacts in a subsequent migration step, then rerun this post-migration audit.

findings.whatIsWrong: Runtime still discovers content/groups/**/*.json and builds simulations from normalized historical groups. It does not load content/taxonomy/pools or a classification manifest.
findings.whyItMatters: The claimed canonical pool selection flow is not active. Historical template groups remain runtime selection boundaries.
findings.recommendedCorrection: After the taxonomy artifacts exist, route simulation allocation through canonical pool indexes and reserve historical groups for provenance or fixed-set resolution only.

findings.whatIsWrong: Ten generated real simulations produced 8 partial selections from historical splittable groups and 3 one-question remnants from historical multi-question groups. One observed Clerical run selected grp-filing-02 as 1/9.
findings.whyItMatters: The original bug remains possible: the simulator can produce one-question remnants labeled by an old Set boundary. The new architecture has not solved the motivating problem.
findings.recommendedCorrection: Replace group-based sampling for pool-like content with compatible canonical-pool sampling. Keep only true atomic/fixed groups whole and contiguous.

findings.whatIsWrong: All 688 question records have no questionType, no questionFormat, and no pool/fixed-group classification fields. Only historical group metadata carries broad questionType values.
findings.whyItMatters: The engine cannot form semantic type blocks for singleton questions, and a future AI cannot determine a canonical destination from the question record or a repository manifest.
findings.recommendedCorrection: Add the claimed row-level classification manifest and wire it into runtime selection. Make questionFormat a controlled vocabulary with compatibility rules.

findings.whatIsWrong: ana-0038 and ana-0040 are explicit letter-series items, but their historical group is labeled questionType Number Sequence. There is no canonical format metadata correcting this.
findings.whyItMatters: A future numeric-only selector could mix or exclude these items incorrectly, and the claimed known correction is not present in the checked-out architecture.
findings.recommendedCorrection: Classify both as letter_sequence in the canonical manifest and keep them out of numeric-only pools.

findings.whatIsWrong: Direct synonym versus synonym-in-context, logical-reasoning formats, and filing formats are not represented as controlled questionFormat metadata. They remain only inferable from subtopic or historical group labels.
findings.whyItMatters: The claimed semantic distinctions cannot be enforced at sampling time and are not a reliable future-AI insertion contract.
findings.recommendedCorrection: Add explicit controlled format values in the classification manifest and validate pool compatibility against them.

findings.whatIsWrong: The build still emits a 602.98 kB minified Firestore chunk and several other chunks above 200 kB; Vite reports a chunk-size warning.
findings.whyItMatters: This is not a taxonomy correctness defect, but it is a scale/performance concern as content and indexes grow.
findings.recommendedCorrection: Measure mobile load performance and establish a bundle budget before adding larger taxonomy indexes.

fixedSets.assessment: The existing eight fixed groups are structurally correct. They are not connected to the claimed missing taxonomy layer.

runtimeAudit.assessment: Fixed groups remain whole, but pool-like groups and singleton questions are still selected through the historical group model; semantic type contiguity is not implemented.

futureAiAudit.destinationForMisspelledWord: Not defined by post-migration artifacts; inferable only from existing docs as Clerical Ability / Spelling.
futureAiAudit.destinationForDirectSynonym: Not defined by post-migration artifacts; inferable only from subtopic/group history.
futureAiAudit.destinationForSynonymInContext: Not defined by post-migration artifacts; inferable only from subtopic/group history.
futureAiAudit.destinationForLetterSequence: Not defined by post-migration artifacts; current group metadata says Number Sequence for ana-0038/0040.
futureAiAudit.destinationForStandaloneTable: Not defined by post-migration artifacts; current record can carry a local passage but no pool classification.
futureAiAudit.assessment: A new AI cannot reliably use the claimed post-migration contract because the contract files are absent.

requiredCorrections: Add content/taxonomy/taxonomy.json with controlled subjects, topics, questionTypes, questionFormats, and compatibility rules.
Add content/taxonomy/classification-manifest.json with exactly 688 unique question IDs and a classification for every question.
Add reference-only semantic pool indexes under content/taxonomy/pools/.
Add content/taxonomy/AI_CONTENT_GUIDE.md with deterministic classification and fixed-set rules.
Change runtime simulation generation to use canonical pool indexes rather than historical pool-like groups.
Ensure pool selection produces contiguous compatible type blocks and cannot create one-question historical-group remnants.
Represent ana-0038 and ana-0040 as letter_sequence and distinguish synonym, logic, and filing formats.
Rerun this post-migration audit after the actual migration artifacts are present.
whatAuditorChanged: No production files changed. Only post-migration audit artifacts will be added.
remaining: The claimed Gemini migration is not present on the audited branch, so the taxonomy is not safe to freeze or use for question 689.
